titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 2/2012 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ސިވިލް އޭވިއޭޝަން އޮތޯރިޓީގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Maldives Civil Aviation Authority Act (Act No. 2/2012). It removes the parts of the Act that give the ministry a role under the old Civil Aviation Act (No. 2/2001) and that make the ministry responsible for civil aviation policy. It tightens the conflict-of-interest rule for board members, shortens the time the board has to meet on an urgent matter from 5 days to 3, and adds permit-issuing and rule-making to the Authority's functions. It also updates the article sending 2 US dollars of each departing passenger's departure tax to the Civil Aviation Fund, and says the right to appeal Authority decisions to the minister applies unless another law says otherwise.
whyItMatters: The Civil Aviation Authority would take over policy and rule-making work from the ministry, and people with any stake in an aviation business could no longer sit on its board.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 removes Article 5(c), which covered doing the ministry's tasks under Act No. 2/2001, and clause 2 removes Article 8, which made the ministry responsible for civil aviation policy and let the minister give the Authority policy directions in writing.

Clause 3 rewrites Article 12(d): a board member must not hold any share or interest in a legal entity that provides civil aviation services, directly or through someone else, or have an interest in any place the Authority regulates. The current rule only bars holdings above 5%.
Clause 4 changes Article 23(b) so that when the Chief Executive asks in writing for an urgent decision, the board must meet and decide within 3 days instead of 5.

Clause 5 adds two items to Article 25: issuing the permits needed to carry out the Authority's duties under this Act or the civil aviation law, and making all regulations needed for its civil aviation responsibilities.

Clause 6 rewrites Article 30 so that 2 US dollars of the departure tax collected from each passenger leaving Maldivian airports goes to the Civil Aviation Fund. The comparison table shows the reference changing from Law No. 71/78 (airport service charge) to Law No. 29/2016 (departure taxes and fees).

Clause 7 rewrites Article 49 so the right to ask the minister to review an Authority decision applies unless another law says otherwise. Clause 8 says the changes take effect once passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: The Civil Aviation Authority and its board, the transport ministry, aviation businesses and people who challenge the Authority's decisions.
statedReasons: The government says these changes are needed to go with a new Maldives Civil Aviation Bill, which would replace Act No. 2/2001 with an up-to-date system for running civil aviation.
